checklist: cert/concurrent.mjs (2.4.9-9, homescoop#712; 2.4.9-10 on slicc-kernel 1.120.2): a ruby process holding an fcntl write lock on pubring.kbx.lock makes gpg --quick-gen-key log 'waiting for lock …pubring.kbx.lock' and finish only after the release (both keys kept); six concurrent gpg --import of distinct keys into a fresh homedir, three rounds as root and one as cone (slicc-bios#496), then into an existing keybox: empty (gpg -k ran once) for one round, and holding six other keys for three rounds as root and one as cone (homescoop#956): every run exits 0 with no error line and every key, imported and held, is kept; four parallel --quick-gen-key in one homedir, as root and cone: every run exits 0 and keeps its key, no lock or keybox errors (no invalid packet / keydb_search tolerance, renames atomic since slicc-kernel 1.117.2), --check-trustdb clean; engines slicc-kernel >=1.117.2. 2.4.9-8: imports fail with 'invalid packet (ctb=00)' and lose keys; 2.4.9-7: gpg doesn't wait (NEGATIVE.md)

cert/concurrent.mjs part 2b (2.4.9-10, homescoop#966): after an import into a keybox, pubring.kbx's st_ino differs from that of a new pubring.kbx.tmp and no pubring.kbx.tmp* file is left (each update has a tmp name of its own; slicc-kernel#954 gives a file created under a just-renamed-away name the renamed file's st_ino); four readers (gpg -k and gpg --list-keys --with-colons) alongside six imports into a keybox holding six keys, three rounds (2.4.9-11, homescoop#1072; slicc-kernel >= 1.124.1 fixes slicc-kernel#980): every read exits 0, logs no error and lists at least the six held keys, and all twelve keys are kept. 2.4.9-9: same st_ino, and readers fail with 'keydb_search_next failed: Provided object is too short' (NEGATIVE.md)

cert/locks.mjs (2.4.9-10, users enforce): cone lists an empty keyring in root's 755 /srv/ro with rc 0, no 'Permission denied' and no lock file there (homescoop#955); after root runs gpg -k and gpg-connect-agent on cone's homedir (no lock files yet, as from 2.4.9-7), pubring.kbx.lock, trustdb.gpg.lock and gnupg_spawn_agent_sentinel.lock are cone's, and cone's --quick-gen-key, --clearsign and --update-trustdb exit 0 with no lock errors; a pubring.kbx.lock/trustdb.gpg.lock that cone symlinks to root's /srv/t/f leaves that file root 644 after root's gpg -k (root gives away only lock files it creates with O_EXCL, regular and with one link); an unlocked root-owned 644 pubring.kbx.lock is replaced by cone's gpg, and all three keys are kept (homescoop#888); after root's gpg imports a key into cone's keybox, pubring.kbx and pubring.kbx~ are cone's, and cone's --quick-gen-key and --clearsign exit 0 with no 'no writable public keyring'; in cone's empty homedir, the pubring.kbx, pubring.kbx~, trustdb.gpg and private-keys-v1.d root's gpg creates are cone's and cone's --quick-gen-key exits 0 (2.4.9-11, homescoop#1031); gpgconf --lock and --unlock say '--lock … not supported on WASI' and fail, never 'invalid size of lockfile' (homescoop#881). 2.4.9-9 fails each part (NEGATIVE.md)
fresh 700 homedir: keybox created, no 'unsafe' ownership warning (st_uid == getuid(), wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-15)
--quick-gen-key default default never (spawns gpg-agent): ed25519 primary, cv25519 subkey, uid
public-key encrypt (PKESK packet 0x84) and decrypt round trip
symmetric -c: right passphrase decrypts; wrong one 'Bad session key', rc 2
--detach-sign checked by gpgv against an exported keyring: Good; tampered file: BAD signature, rc 1

cert/modes.mjs (wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-17 + slicc-kernel 1.35.1 slicc_fs): default ~/.gnupg 700, private-keys-v1.d 700, both .key 600, trustdb.gpg 600, openpgp-revocs.d 700 and its .rev 600, pubring.kbx 644 (umask, as on Linux); a 755 homedir gets gpg's 'unsafe permissions' warning

cert/users.mjs (2.4.9-5, H1 homescoop#207, wasix-sysroot -20, slicc-kernel >= 1.47.1): as root and as kernel.users.add cone, gpg creates ~/.gnupg and a key with no 'unsafe ownership/permissions' warning; ~/.gnupg is '<user> 700' (coreutils 9.12.0-5 stat names the owner); list-keys shows one uid; chmod 755 on the homedir makes gpg warn 'unsafe permissions on homedir'. engines slicc-kernel >= 1.47.1: gpg compares the homedir owner with getuid(), and only 1.47.1 reports owners as the caller's ids

cert/agent-signals.mjs (2.4.9-6, wasix-sysroot -28: npth_pselect with a signal mask, slicc-kernel 1.93.0): gpg-agent started by gpg-connect-agent with log-file + verbose; kill -HUP logs 'SIGHUP received - re-reading configuration and flushing cache' and the same pid keeps answering 'getinfo pid'; kill -TERM logs 'SIGTERM received - shutting down' and the agent is gone (kill -0 fails) within 5 s; a new agent's kill -INT logs 'SIGINT received - immediate shutdown' and it exits; package.json names wasix-sysroot -34 (2.4.9-10; -28 from 2.4.9-6). 2.4.9-5 (sysroot -20) passes it too on the Node entry: the masked-wait race is the sysroot's r28w case; the delta row is the toolchain record (NEGATIVE.md)
